properties.decision:
**RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL.** Anthony, 2026-08-29, from research he did while the stale-server fix was being built.

THE IDEA: run `cargo watch -x build` beside a development session, so a source change rebuilds the binary without anyone asking.

⭐ IT IS ORTHOGONAL TO WHAT SHIPPED, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE POINT OF RECORDING IT. `cap:a-client-elects-a-server-of-its-own-build` makes the next tool call pick up a NEW BINARY automatically; it does not make the binary. `cargo-watch` makes the binary; it does not touch the daemon. Together the loop closes end to end — edit, rebuild, next call serves it — and neither half does the other's job.

🛑 DEV TOOLING, NOT PRODUCT. This would never ship to a user: a consumer installs a release binary and has no source tree, so `cargo-watch` cannot reach the case Alex reported. Recording that boundary is half the value of the node, because the two problems look identical and have different audiences.

TWO OTHER OPTIONS FROM THE SAME RESEARCH, KEPT SO THEY ARE NOT RE-PROPOSED:

**`mcp-server-hmr` / `mcpmon`** — an external supervisor that watches the binary and swaps the process while keeping the stdio stream alive. ⭐ ITS SHAPE IS EXACTLY WHAT SHIPPED, which is a point in the design's favour rather than against the tool: the same mechanism, placed INSIDE reflow2 so no user installs npm or edits an MCP config. ⚠️ Counter: it also covers the case where the process wedges rather than merely being stale, which the re-election does not.

**Hard-reloading the client** (`Cmd+Shift+R`, `Developer: Reload Window`) — 🛑 THIS ONE DOES NOT WORK HERE AND THE REASON IS ON THE RECORD. It kills ATTACHED CHILD processes, and `--serve-shared` is detached on purpose. `fact:the-stale-server-defect-recurred-to-the-people-who-wrote-it-down` measured exactly this on 2026-08-08: *"every session that restarted RE-ATTACHED TO THE SAME STALE PROCESS."* It is the documented-remedy-that-is-not, in a new costume, and it is written down here so nobody reaches for it again.

⚠️ THE HONEST COUNTER TO THE WHOLE IDEA: the shipped fix may make it unnecessary in practice. The pain being solved was six lost cycles in one session, and every one of those was *the daemon did not follow the rebuild* rather than *the rebuild did not happen* — a human ran `cargo build` each time. Auto-rebuild removes a keystroke, not a defect. Worth trying for a session before adopting it, rather than installing a global tool on an argument.
properties.name: OPEN — should the dev loop use cargo-watch, now that a client re-elects on a rebuild by itself?
properties.rationale:
Captured under the brainstorm skill: recorded AS AN IDEA, with the options and their counters, and nothing promoted. It arrived as research rather than as a request to build, and the difference is worth preserving.

⭐ THE PART MOST WORTH KEEPING IS THE ONE THAT WAS REFUTED. Hard-reloading the client is the obvious move, it is what the ecosystem advises, and it is wrong here for a structural reason — the daemon is deliberately detached. That is already a measured finding from 2026-08-08, and without this node the next person to research the problem finds the same advice and tries it, because the advice is correct for ordinary MCP servers and reflow2 is not one.

WHY IT IS NOT PROMOTED NOW: `dec:the-hub-waits-for-somebody-to-ask-for-it` was settled hours earlier on the principle that a thing nobody is asking for waits. This is smaller and cheaper than the hub, but the same test applies — and unusually, the person who would benefit is the maintainer himself, so the demand signal is available for free the next time a session loses a cycle to a stale build. If that stops happening now that the client re-elects, the idea has answered itself.
